title: A Product Manager's Real Week: One Support Ticket to a Buildable Plan
description:
What does a product manager actually do all week? We walk through one real Monday-to-Friday on a SaaS product's notifications area: reading support tickets, interviewing a churned user, writing a one-page problem statement, fighting for engineering time, and drafting the spec. Notice what never happens: no code, no final design, no sprint timeline. The PM's job is turning a noisy signal into a defined, prioritized, buildable plan.

Source lesson(s):
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/01-what-is-product-management/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Here's one real week for a product manager. No code, no mockups. Just turning a messy signal into a plan the team can build.

display.heading: A Day in the Life of a PM

beats.narration: Monday, they read weekend support tickets and spot three complaints about duplicate email digests. Tuesday, a call with a user who churned, citing notification overload. They're hunting for a pattern, not a one-off.

display.heading: Monday & Tuesday: gather the signal
display.subheading: Three duplicate-digest complaints. One churned user citing notification overload.

beats.narration: Wednesday, they write a one-page problem statement and take it to prioritization, where it competes with two other ideas. Thursday, they draft the spec for the winner, a digest-frequency setting.

display.heading: Wednesday & Thursday: define and prioritize
display.subheading: A one-page problem statement vs. two other initiatives for a two-engineer team.

beats.narration: Friday, they present the expected impact to the head of product. Notice what never happened: no code, no design, no timeline. The PM turned noise into a buildable plan. That's the job.

display.heading: Friday: align on the plan
display.subheading: No code, no pixel-level design, no sprint timeline -- a noisy signal became a buildable plan.

beats.narration: Want the full week-by-week breakdown? It's in lesson one of the Product Manager Mastery Path.
